references.text: Further instructions on applying the blood to the doorframes with hyssop, and the promise that the Lord will pass over and protect against the destroyer.
The blood shall be a sign on the houses, and the Lord will pass by when he sees the blood, so that no destroying plague may strike them.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to Passover and the application of blood as an act of faith; by faith Moses kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood.
Blood is used in the cleansing ritual for leprosy, applied in a similar manner as a purifying and protective agent.
The prophet Ezekiel describes that blood shall be smeared on the doorposts of the temple as part of the cleansing ritual.
Isaiah mentions doorposts (mezuzot) in a context contrasting idolatry with true worship.
Peter's first letter speaks of being chosen for obedience and to be cleansed by the blood of Jesus Christ, fulfilling the symbolism of the Passover blood.
The holy ones have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb, a parallel to protection through the blood at Passover.
Directly related verses in the same event explaining the purpose of the blood: the Lord's passing over and protection from judgment.
Direct instruction completing the picture of the ritual in the source verse; describes the method (hyssop) and the warning to remain inside.
